value: What is known about the structure of science collaboration networks in sociology, and how developed are the co-authorship networks of sociologists in Serbia?

Reviews earlier work on collaboration-network structure in sociology and adds a bibliometric count of single-author versus co-authored papers in three Serbian sociology journals (2000–2010), concluding that co-authorship networks among Serbian sociologists are weakly developed.

quote: We have analysed coauthors’ works according to the criterion of belonging to the same or different scientific/educational institution.
Based on this insight, we can conclude that the scientific networks of coauthors’ works of sociologists in Serbia are not quite developed.
Science collaboration networks occupy an important place in the analysis of social networks.

value: 1990s isolation and economic collapse produced minimal science funding and minimal international contact, which suppressed the coauthorship that funding and contact would otherwise generate
quote: Among all else, it produced minimal investment in science, as well as hard and minimal international cooperation.

value: projects framed around very general themes let each associate work on his own issue without leaving his own profession, so participation never turns into joint problem-solving and hence not into coauthorship
quote: Problems related to the project are mostly chosen based on such general notion which could enable the project work of the associates who could tackle various issues, without the obligation to step out of their own profession.

value: Across three Serbian sociology journals for 2000-2010, single-authored papers overwhelmingly dominate: 89.1% of published texts against only 10.9% coauthored.

value: Among the coauthored papers, collaboration between colleagues in the same institution is twice as frequent as collaboration across institutions.
quote: The conclusion is that the participation of coauthors who are employed in the same institutions is twice as higher than the participation of the authors who cooperate with the colleagues from the other scientific institutions (see table 1).

value: The authors conclude from these frequencies that coauthorship networks among Serbian sociologists are underdeveloped.

value: Serbian sociologists at the start of the 21st century collaborated three times less than the sociologists in Moody's international data.
quote: Therefore, it does not come as a surprise that the cooperation of the Serbian sociologists at the beginning of the 21st century was three times smaller than the cooperation of the sociologists portrayed in Moody’s research.

value: Kronegger and colleagues, applying the same methodology as Moody, arrive at a different network structure for sociology, which the authors attribute to the size of the national scientific community and its dependence on ministry funding.
quote: Even though Kronegger and his associates used the same methodology as Moody did, we have seen that the results of their research point out different network structures which are realised by the sociologists.

value: Although sociology is taught at three Serbian universities, none of their study programmes contains a course on the theory or analysis of social networks.
quote: there is not one subject which is dedicated to the theory and analysis of social networks in their study programmes.

value: In all four Slovenian disciplines examined, scientists preferentially form new coauthorships with the coauthors of their coauthors, closing triangles - a signature of small-world clustering within network borders.
quote: In all four disciplines, scientists are inclined to form new coauthorship connections with coauthors of their coauthors, which is irrefutable confirmation of high grouping inside network borders and a clear indicator of small-world network structures.
